clue.text: Settles in or out of court

definitions.text: Settles in or out of court

parts.words: Settles in or out of court
parts.note: a settle is a long wooden seat; the court's judicial seat and the long seats outside on a playing court or in a corridor are all of this kind

explanation.surface: Legal disputes are resolved either before a judge or by private agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settles' reads as a verb about lawsuits, but it is a plural noun: settles are long seats, found both in a courtroom and outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a long seat with a high back, so several settles are long seats of that kind.

clue.text: Ordered brigade to abandon equipment

indicators.note: the word brigade is made to give up a run of its letters, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: rig means equipment or gear, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A military unit was commanded to leave its kit behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the past tense of bid, so it means ordered or commanded someone to do something.

clue.text: A time when there are most strikes?

definitions.text: A time when there are most strikes?

parts.words: A time when there are most strikes?
parts.note: a striking clock chimes twelve times at midday, the largest number of strokes in its cycle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' suggests industrial action, but it means the chimes of a clock, which strikes twelve at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is when a clock strikes twelve, the most chimes of any hour.

clue.text: In which all entrants won't come up to scratch

definitions.text: In which all entrants won't come up to scratch

parts.words: In which all entrants won't come up to scratch
parts.note: in a race or golf event with allowances, competitors start from different marks rather than all from the scratch line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come up to scratch' means be good enough, but scratch here is the zero-allowance mark in golf or the starting line of a race, which weaker entrants do not start from.
explanation.definitionFit: A race or competition where weaker contestants get an allowance so that not everyone starts from scratch.

clue.text: An accident to make light of

definitions.meaning: a fall or tumble, as from a horse or bike, or liquid knocked over
a thin twist of paper or sliver of wood used to light a fire or pipe

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a mishap as nothing serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' means play down, but here it means something used to make a flame: a paper or wood taper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumble or fall is a mishap, and a taper of rolled paper used for lighting is the same word.

clue.text: Despicable person possibly got time inside

indicators.note: the time word is placed within the jumbled letters
signals that the letters of got may be rearranged into another order

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A villain probably ended up doing a stretch in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got time inside' reads as a prison sentence, which hides the container. Toerag is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is British slang for a worthless or contemptible person, a low scoundrel.

clue.text: Oil producers under pressure have hearts of stone

definitions.text: Oil producers under pressure have hearts of stone

parts.words: Oil producers under pressure have hearts of stone
parts.note: fruits pressed to yield oil, each with a stone at its centre

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hard-hearted oil executives, but it describes small stoned fruits crushed in a press to make oil.
explanation.definitionFit: These stone fruits are pressed for their oil and each has a hard pit at its core.

clue.text: It helps the dough go further

definitions.text: It helps the dough go further

parts.words: It helps the dough go further
parts.note: a kitchen tool spreads pastry dough out thinner and wider

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making the dough go further' sounds like stretching money, but the dough is pastry, rolled out flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cylinder rolled over pastry spreads the dough out over a larger area.

clue.text: A pet gun dog involved in drive

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A family dog gets caught up in a shooting trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A PET GUN DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is energy and enterprise, the same as drive or ambition.

clue.text: Proverbially, no longer a stud

parts.note: the large-headed nail studding an old door features in the saying 'dead as a ...'

explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer a stud' hints at a retired breeding horse; the proverb is 'dead as a doornail', a stud on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'dead as a doornail' makes this door stud proverbially lifeless.

clue.text: A boring cocktail?

parts.note: a drink of gin and lime shares its name with a small hand tool for drilling holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but it means drilling: the drink shares its name with a hand tool for boring holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin-and-lime drink that is also a small hand drill for boring holes.

clue.text: One way to loaf is to walk leisurely

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a roll is a small single loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Loafing about is a matter of walking without hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like a verb meaning idle, but it is the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is an unhurried walk, and to stroll is to amble.

clue.text: White pillows can be something hard to get hold of

definitions.text: something hard to get hold of

indicators.note: signals that the letters of white pillows can be turned into something else

explanation.surface: Bedding that slips away whenever you grab it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges WHITE PILLOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A will-o'-the-wisp is a marsh light or anything elusive that cannot be caught.

clue.text: Flags put out in honour to a brave man

definitions.meaning: bunting hung up for a celebration is ornamentation

explanation.surface: Banners are hung to celebrate a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental bunting is festive adornment, and a medal for valour is also called this.

clue.text: Class total needs adjusting, whatever the consequences

indicators.note: the letters of class total must be rearranged to fix them

explanation.surface: A school's headcount must be corrected no matter what happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs adjusting' rearranges CLASS TOTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless of price or risk, no matter what.

clue.text: The strain of dental treatment

definitions.meaning: a line of descent or ancestry, as in 'of Irish stock'
the pulling out of a tooth

explanation.surface: Having a tooth pulled is a stressful ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress, but it means lineage or stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or lineage is one sense; the pulling of a tooth is another.

clue.text: Regrettable comment on unsatisfactory work

definitions.meaning: a teacher's remark on poor homework, saying it is excessively poor

explanation.surface: A teacher writes a sorry remark on a poor essay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unfortunate, and literally says work is excessively poor.

clue.text: Type of trap still produced in Holland

definitions.meaning: a spirit distilled by the Dutch as genever

explanation.surface: A Dutch contraption for catching animals is still made there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'even now', but it is a distilling apparatus: genever, Dutch spirit, is made in a still.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin trap is an animal snare, and the juniper spirit originated as Dutch genever.

clue.text: The top pub in the place, perhaps

indicators.note: the pub word is placed within the jumbled letters
signals the letters of place may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: The finest pub in town, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The place' suggests one particular spot, but 'perhaps' signals a reshuffle of its second word, the jumble then cut open by 'in' to take the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a peak or summit, the highest point.

clue.text: Bird cry as heard in the East End

indicators.text: as heard in the East End
indicators.note: Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop the h at the start of words

parts.note: a howl is a long loud cry

explanation.surface: A bird's call as spoken by a Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally Cockney part of London, where speakers drop initial h, so a cry loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal bird of prey with large eyes is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Employment in which workers were paid to unpick seams

definitions.text: Employment in which workers were paid to unpick seams

parts.words: Employment in which workers were paid to unpick seams
parts.note: seams are underground layers of fuel which colliers dug out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpick seams' suggests needlework, but the seams are layers of coal hewn out with picks.
explanation.definitionFit: Colliery work involves extracting fuel from underground seams with picks.

clue.text: Designer label excited Marian

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman gets thrilled about a fashion brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges MARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is an Italian fashion designer whose name is a famous label.

clue.text: Confirming seating in car trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Checking the seat arrangement for a car journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey, but it signals a stumble that rearranges SEATING IN CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, so ascertaining is establishing or confirming.

clue.text: Words of love among sisters

indicators.note: the love letter is placed in the midst of the sisters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Affectionate words exchanged among siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouns are naming words, a class of words in grammar.

clue.text: Childishly claims the luggage

definitions.meaning: children say '... I' to claim something first
cases and holdalls carried when travelling

explanation.surface: A child stakes a claim to the suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is British children's slang for claiming first right to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's claiming slang and a word for suitcases and holdalls.

clue.text: Grasping what is meant by average

definitions.meaning: to intend or signify, as in 'what I intend'
the arithmetic middle value of a set of numbers

explanation.surface: Getting hold of what 'average' signifies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasping' looks like understanding, but it means miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is stingy, to intend is to signify, and the average is a statistical middle.

clue.text: Establish there's point in new Latin

indicators.note: the point letter goes within the rearranged Latin
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of Latin

parts.note: S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: Introducing a fresh spot in a revised Latin text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns LATIN into INTAL, and 'in' puts S inside. Instal is a variant spelling of install.
explanation.definitionFit: To instal is to set up or install, to establish someone or something in place.

clue.text: Buy tea in a bag

indicators.note: the tea word sits within the bag word

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Get some tea sold in a sachet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea in a bag' suggests a teabag; CHA is a slang word for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to acquire something by paying money for it.

clue.text: Monster is seen swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A lake creature has been spotted in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges IS SEEN. NESSIE is the legendary Loch Ness monster in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the nickname of the Loch Ness Monster, a legendary Scottish creature.

clue.text: Boards with relative by marriage

definitions.meaning: gets on a vehicle, as in walking up and on to a bus
a spouse's son from a previous relationship

explanation.surface: Someone takes in an in-law as a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, STEPS ON, to get the sense 'boards'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's child from an earlier relationship becomes a relative by marriage.
